ACCIDENT RELEASE PREVENTION AND RESPONSE POLICIES
Montare Operating, LTD (Montare) owns and operates a natural gas processing plant, the Hainesville Gas Processing Plant in Wood County, Texas, that receives, stores, and transfers petroleum. The facility is designed to process liquefied petroleum gas by fractionation into end products that will be delivered to end markets. 

Montare has a long-standing commitment to workers and public safety. This commitment is demonstrated by our efforts in accident prevention, such as training personnel, quality assurance, and considering safety in the design, installation, operation, and maintenance of our process. Our policy is to implement reasonable controls to prevent foreseeable releases of regulated substances. However, if a release does occur, facility-trained personnel will evaluate the situation, take actions within the capabilities of the facility, and notify the necessary outside agencies.

DESCRIPTION OF THE STATIONARY SOURCE AND REGULATED SUBSTANCE
The Hainesville Gas Processing Plant is located near Hainesville, Texas and operates a variety of processes to produce the following  products: 
1. Ethane
2. Propane
3. Butane
4. Isobutane
5. Natural Gas (C5+)

The received Liquefied Petroleum Gas and produced products can contain the following components:
a. Methane
b. Ethane
c. Propane
d. Butane
e. Isobutane
f. Pentane
g. Isopentane
h. Carbons larger than C5+

GENERAL ACCIDENT RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM 
A. Employee Participation
Montare encourages employees to participate in all facets of process safety management and accident prevention as follows:
1. Updating and compiling technical documents and chemical information
2. Performing necessary calculations for PSM and RMP
3. Maintaining good engineering practices
4. Participating as a member of a process hazard analysis (PHA) team

Employees have access to all information pertaining to the accident prevention program.

B. Process Safety Information
Montare keeps a variety

of technical documents that are used to help maintain safe operation of the processes. These technical documents address the following:
1. Chemical properties and associated hazards
2. Necessary Block Flow Diagrams of the process
3. Maximum intended inventories
4. Upper and Lower limits of process fixed and rotating equipment
5. Equipment design basis and configuration information
6. Identification of all necessary Regulatory equipment design documents
7. Sufficient information to assure good engineering practices

The location of the technical documents referenced above is listed in the Process Safety Information portion of the PSM.
Chemical-specific information, including hazard and emergency response/exposure considerations, is provided in safety data sheets (SDS). For specific process areas, the facility has documented safety-related limits for specific process parameters such as temperatures, level, and composition in the operators' procedures manual. The facility maintains the process within these limits by using process controls and monitoring instruments, trained personnel and protective instrument systems such as automated shutdown systems.
The facility also maintains numerous technical documents that provide information about the design and construction of the process equipment. This information includes materials of construction, design pressures, temperature, and electrical ratings. This information, in combination with procedures and equipment operating history, provides a basis for inspection and maintenance activities, as well as for evaluating proposed process and facility changes to the safety features in the process are not compromised.

C. Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) 
Montare has a comprehensive program to identify and control hazards associated with the RMP-covered process. This program systematically examines for potential hazards and puts controls in place to manage hazards. The team identifies, evaluates, and makes recommendations to manage

ment of potential hazards identified. The team's findings are forwarded to Montare's management for resolution. The approved mitigation options in response to the PHA team's findings are tracked until they are completed. The final resolution of each finding is documented and retained.
The facility periodically updates and revalidates the hazard analysis results. These periodic reviews are conducted at least every 5 years and will be conducted at this frequency until the process is no longer operating. The results and findings from these updates are documented and retained.

D. Operating Procedures
Montare maintains written Operating Procedures of the covered process that address primary operations mandated by OSHA, EPA, Good Engineering Practice, and equipment manufacturers. These procedures can be used as a reference by experienced operators and provide a basis for consistent training of new operators. Procedures are periodically reviewed and annually certified as current and accurate by management. The procedures are maintained current and accurate, revising them as necessary by employee's suggestion, compliance audit, PHAs, Good Engineering Practice, and Pre-Startup Safety Review (PSSR) and are implemented through the Management of Change process.
Covered Process Operating procedures are readily available to operators in the process unit and for other personnel to use as necessary to safely perform their job task and maintain the covered process unit operating within its safe limits.

E. Training
Montare has implemented a comprehensive training program for all employees involved in operating the covered process. New employees receive basic training in process operations if they are not already familiar with such operations. After successfully completing this training, a new operator is paired with a senior operator to learn process-specific duties and tasks. A performance review must be successfully completed during this training period. After the operator demons

trates adequate knowledge to perform the duties and tasks in a safe manner on their own, they are allowed to work independently. In addition, all operators periodically receive refresher training on the operating procedures to ensure that their skills and knowledge are maintained at an acceptable level. This refresher training is conducted at least every 3 years, or more frequently upon request. All training is documented for each operator, including the means used to verify and demonstrate skills.

F. Contractors
Montare uses contractors to supplement its workforce during periods of increased maintenance or construction activities. Because some contractors work on or near covered process equipment, the facility has procedures in place to ensure that contractors: 
1. Perform their work in a safe manner
2. Have the appropriate knowledge and skills
3. Are aware of the hazards in their workplace
4. Understand what they should do in the event of an emergency
5. Understand and follow site safety rules
6. Inform facility personnel of any hazard that they find during their work

This is accomplished by providing contractors with:
1. A process overview
2. Information about safety and health hazards
3. Emergency response plan requirements
4. Safe work practices before beginning work

In addition, Montare management will evaluate the contractor safety program and performance during the selection of a contractor. Facility personnel periodically monitor contractor performance with regard to their safety obligations.

G. Pre-Startup Safety Review (PSSR)
Montare conducts a PSSR for any new facility modification that requires a change in the process safety information. The purpose of the PSSR is to see that safety features, procedures, personnel, and equipment are appropriately prepared for startup before placing the equipment into service. This review provides one additional check that construction is in accordance with the design specifications and that all supporting systems ar

e operationally ready. A PSSR involves field verification of the construction and services as quality assurance verification that the accident prevention program requirements are properly implemented.

H. Mechanical Integrity
Montare has established practices and procedures for the safe operation of fixed, rotating, and emergency shutdown equipment. The basic aspects of the program include, but are not limited to, the following: 
1. Conducting training
2. Developing written procedures
3. Performing inspections and tests
4. Correcting identified deficiencies
5. Applying quality assurance measures

In combination, these activities form a system to maintain the mechanical integrity of the process. Maintenance personnel receive training on: 
1. Overview of the process
2. Safety and Health hazards
3. Applicable maintenance procedures
4. Emergency response plan
5. Applicable safe work practices to help ensure that they can perform their jobs in a safe manner.

Written procedures provide that work is performed in a consistent manner and serve as a basis for training. Inspections and tests are performed to help verify that equipment functions as intended and that equipment is within acceptable limits. If a deficiency is identified and the situation presents an immediate safety concern, the deficiency is corrected before placing the equipment back into service. A management of change team will review the use of equipment and determine what action is necessary.
An integral part of the mechanical integrity program is quality assurance. Montare incorporates quality assurance measures into equipment purchases and repairs. This helps to determine that new equipment is suitable for its intended use and that the proper materials and spare parts are used when repairs are made.

I. Safe Work Practices
Montare has standing safe work practices in place as mandated by OSHA, EPA, Industrial Standards, and Good Engineering Practice to help provide employee, public, and process safety.

J.

Management of Change
Montare has a comprehensive system to manage changes to all Reported Covered Processes. This system requires that changes to items such as process equipment, chemicals, technology, and procedures be properly reviewed and authorized before being implemented. Changes are reviewed to: 
1. Determine that adequate controls are in place to manage any new hazards
2. Verify that existing controls have not been compromised by the proposed change

Affected chemical hazard information, process operating limits, and equipment information and procedures are updated to incorporate these changes. In addition, operating and maintenance personnel are trained on the changes.

K. Incident Investigation
Montare will promptly investigate all incidents related to a covered process that resulted in, or reasonably could have resulted in a fire/explosion, property damage, environmental loss or personal injury. The goal of each investigation will be to determine the facts and develop corrective action to prevent a recurrence of the incident or a similar incident. The investigation team will document its findings, develop recommendations to prevent future occurrences, and forward these results to facility management for resolution. Corrective actions taken in response to the investigation team's findings and recommendations will be tracked until they are complete. The final resolution of each finding or recommendation will be documented, and investigation reports will be retained for at least 5 years. 

L. Compliance Audits
At least every 3 years a Compliance Audit addressing OSHA, EPA, RMP, and Good Engineering Practices is conducted by employees and management of Montare. This audit team develops findings that are forwarded to facility management for resolution. Corrective actions taken in response to the audit team's findings are tracked until they are completed. The final resolution of each finding is documented, and the two most recent audit reports are retained.

M

. Chemical-Specific Prevention Steps
Montare's accident release prevention and response policies are applied to all RMP-covered processes. Collectively, these prevention program activities help prevent potential accident scenarios that could be caused by equipment failures and human errors.

N. Specialized Safety Features
Site-specific detection and control equipment (safety features) are deployed throughout the plant to:
1. Contain/control a release,
2. Quickly detect a release, and
3. Reduce the consequences of an RMP-regulated substance release

The following types of safety features are used in the covered process: 
Release Detection
1. Process relief valves that discharge to a flare to capture and incinerate episodic releases
2. Automatic and manual valves to permit isolation of the process
3. Automatic plant shutdown system to shut down all engines, plant utilities and automatically operate all automatic valves to their fail-safe position, diverting all incoming gas to the emergency flare. 
4. Curing or diking to contain liquids releases
5. Redundant equipment and instrumentation
6. Atmospheric relief devices 
7. Camera and audiovisual monitoring of the site
8. Process area and perimeter CGA monitors and alarms

Release Mitigation
1. Fire extinguishers
2. Trained emergency response personnel
3. Personal protective equipment

O. FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY
The Hainesville Gas Processing Plant has had no RMP-regulated substance releases during the past five years. 

P. EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM INFORMATION
The plant maintains a written emergency action plan which is in place to help protect employees and public safety as well as the environment. The plan identifies steps to be taken in case of an accidental release including proper first aid and medical treatment for exposures, evacuation plans and accounting for personnel after an evacuation, notification of local emergency response agencies and the public if a release occurs.
Employees receive training in the

procedures to be followed by employees who remain to operate critical plant operations before they evacuate. Montare has around-the-clock communications capability with appropriate emergency response organizations (Fire Department, Police, Sheriff's Office, or similar). This interface provides the means of notifying the public of an incident, if necessary, as well as facilitating quick response to an incident. In addition, Montare conducts periodic emergency drills and annual refresher training for plant personnel.

Q. Planned changes to improve safety
Montare's management is committed to the following:
1. Preventing accidents
2. Training our employees in correct response procedures in the event of an accident
3. Participating in community emergency preparedness
4. Addressing any citizen concerns by fully explaining potential hazards associated with Montare operations and all steps being taken to prevent and mitigate accidents.

With these objectives in mind, this Risk Management Plan has been developed to provide information about our management of the risks associated with the natural gas treatment and liquids recovery process. Most importantly, we stress our commitment to ensuring a safe operation for our employees, our visitors, and our community.
